operations.comment: ; Sixteen-byte iNES header: MMC1 cartridge, 128 KiB PRG and 128 KiB CHR; no trainer. Header values are preserved exactly.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks in CPU slots $8000/$A000/$C000/$E000: [0, 1, 14, 15]. Null slots remain unresolved.

; Double A to select paired pointers in nine tables and install resource bases in zero-page $AB..$BC. These include spawn/script families, frame/width and CHR-compatibility columns. Independent six-cell table boundaries are supported; natural area selection and some original resource names remain unresolved.

; Six little-endian pointers per column select resource bases through the PRG-pair-zero area loader. Nine adjacent columns have independent bases; the original global area-selector domain remains unresolved.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks ($8000/$A000/$C000/$E000): [[0, 1, 14, 15]].
; Use area selector bits 4..5 and the player position to prepare display values in $2F/$31/$33. The coordinate lookup uses the full Y selector; callers must supply the established finite area domain.
; 48 area-dependent coordinate values. Finite fields and boundaries follow the saved consumer and neighboring-record review; this does not assert natural selector coverage.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks ($8000/$A000/$C000/$E000): [[0, 1, 14, 15]].

; Unpack the two input BCD bytes at $2F/$30 into four low-first decimal digits, zero the remaining two addend digits, and add into the six unpacked score digits at $04DE. Carry is implemented explicitly because the NES has no decimal arithmetic; overflow beyond digit six is discarded. F1E1 selects physical PRG banks 0/1 for this call; the same CPU address in PRG pair six is a different routine.
; Walk six low-first digits, subtract ten on overflow and propagate carry into the next digit. The addend scratch has two zero high digits.
; Continue with clear carry when the current decimal sum is below ten.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks ($8000/$A000/$C000/$E000): [[0, 1, 14, 15]].

; Add A to the decimal pair at $04C6/$04C7. Carry past 99 increments the shared saturated pair at $04C4/$04C5. The neighboring entry points increment, decrement or add to other decimal pairs; callers supply small decimal addends, not arbitrary binary bytes.
; Increment the shared low/high decimal pair, saturating at 99. Decimal overflow from the other add helpers also enters here.
; Subtract one from the decimal pair, borrowing through the high digit and clamping underflow to zero. Return A=1 at zero, A=0 otherwise.
; Add A to the second decimal pair with decimal carry into the shared pair on overflow. Once its high digit reaches four, clear its low digit as encoded; do not assume an ordinary modulo-100 counter.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks ($8000/$A000/$C000/$E000): [[0, 1, 14, 15]].
; Subtract A units and Y tens from the two unpacked credit digits at $04C8/$04C9. Borrow adds ten to the units; negative tens clamps both digits to zero.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks in CPU slots $8000/$A000/$C000/$E000: [0, 1, 14, 15]. Null slots remain unresolved.

; Use the descending frame byte to sample state entries: only ticks below $30 are eligible, masked with $2F, excluding the two active area selectors. Increment the sampled low nibble toward five and set its high flag. The game meaning of this per-area counter is unresolved.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks ($8000/$A000/$C000/$E000): [[0, 1, 14, 15]].

; Add A to the low decimal digit at $04CA; propagate decimal carry into $04CB and saturate both digits to nine on overflow. The caller supplies a decimal addend small enough for one normalization per digit.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks ($8000/$A000/$C000/$E000): [[0, 1, 14, 15]].
; Subtract A from the two digits at $04CA/$04CB with decimal borrow and clamp at zero. Separate entries below add to or subtract from $04E7/$04E8; addition saturates at 99.
; Add A to the two unpacked digits at $04E7/$04E8. Propagate the units carry and saturate overflow to 99.
; Subtract A from $04E7/$04E8 using decimal borrow; clamp negative results to zero.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks ($8000/$A000/$C000/$E000): [[0, 1, 14, 15]].
; Increment $04E5 up to nine. This is a bounded counter; its precise inventory meaning is unresolved.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks ($8000/$A000/$C000/$E000): [[0, 1, 14, 15]].
; Decrement $04E5 when nonzero; the zero case returns through the preceding RTS.

; Seventeen little-endian scene-descriptor pointers selected by the fixed loader after selecting PRG pair zero. The first pointed five-byte record independently bounds this array; natural selector range remains unresolved.

; Repeated small-value sequences and low-valued fields establish this bounded non-code interval. Current-source references, indexed bases and immediate neighbors were inspected in the saved round001 redirect pattern review, and exact final bounds rechecked in round002. The consumer and original record/container layout remain unresolved; these bytes are generic Data.

; Little-endian descriptor pointers indexed by the PRG-pair-zero upload loader. The first cell is null. Twenty pointed seven-byte descriptors are supported; the last apparent pointer reaches executable palette code and is not a valid extra descriptor.

; Seven-byte records contain bank, two-byte output length, source pointer and optional two-byte PPU destination. The fixed upload loader reads these fields; adjacent records end at independently established palette code.
; This physical emission may be a slice of an overlapping consumer footprint; its boundary does not imply a separate original resource.
; Effective physical 8 KiB PRG banks in CPU slots $8000/$A000/$C000/$E000: [0, 1, 14, 15]. Null slots remain unresolved.

; A and X select two 16-byte palettes through pointer tables; combine them into the 32-byte working palette and initialize the split-screen colors. The following entries preserve target colors and animate brightness/emphasis.
; Save the complete palette as the target and reduce current colors to their low nibbles. Start emphasis and brightness restoration.
; First remove emphasis in four stages; then add $10 to each color until its saved target is reached. A=1 marks the completed stage, A=0 requests another frame.
; Decrease each non-dark color by $10, then increase emphasis stages. Reload palette zero and synchronize at completion.
; Four palette emphasis masks. Finite fields and boundaries follow the saved consumer and neighboring-record review; this does not assert natural selector coverage.

; Paired palette-source pointers read by the PRG-pair-zero palette loader. Separate encoded table bases and the earliest payload bound these arrays. Null cells are retained without claiming they select a palette.

; The palette loader copies sixteen bytes from each selected source into the working palette. Some encoded values exceed $3F; this is the consumed representation, without a canonical six-bit color-domain claim.
; This physical emission may be a slice of an overlapping consumer footprint; its boundary does not imply a separate original resource.
